newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN council chief hopes Iraq oil to flow this month.
newsitem.headline: UN council chief hopes Iraq oil to flow this month.

text.p: Security Council President Francesco Fulci of Italy said Tuesday he hoped the long-delayed "oil-food-food" deal with Iraq would begin to be implemented during December and stressed the urgency of carrying out the plan.

He was referring to an agreement signed by the United Nations and Iraq in May providing for the sale of $2 billion of Iraqi oil over six months, on a renewable basis, to buy food, medicine and other humanitarian goods to offset the effects of sanctions imposed since Iraq's August 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
The last impediments to carrying out the plan were removed November 25 when Iraq finally agreed to all U.N. conditions.
"The oil-for-food (deal)...hopefully will begin to be implemented this month, December," Fulci told reporters after private security council consultations.
"We are waiting for a final report from the secretary-general because he has the authority to decide when the conditions are in place to start with the operation," Fulci said.
Fulci serves as the security council's president during December.
He said a report was due by the end of this week at the latest from a group of experts who have been examining a pipeline from Iraq to Turkey, through which the bulk of the oil is due to flow.
"Then we shall be waiting anxiously for the secretary-general to give the signal," he said.
He said he used the word "anxiously" because "every day of delay in the implementation of this resolution means death by a terrible disease....starvation.
"We do hope therefore that not one day will be lost in its implementation to save innocent, and I underline innocent, human life."
